newsitem.title: USA: Lucent meets Q2 promises of higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Lucent meets Q2 promises of higher profits.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc reported solid earnings and revenue growth at the high end of the range the company had projected two weeks ago for its second fiscal quarter ended March 31.
The leading U.S. telecom equipment supplier said net income for the March quarter was $66 million, or $0.10 per share, versus a loss of $103 million, or $0.16, a year-ago.
The company said revenues of $5.15 billion were up 12.5 percent from a year ago, while revenues from continuing operations were up 16.1 percent on a comparable basis.

On April 3, Lucent Chief Financial Officer Donald Peterson told analysts in a conference call he expected net income in the range of $55 to $66 million, or $0.09 to $0.10 a share, more than double the analysts' consensus estimate at the time.

Thursday, Lucent said revenues for systems for network operators rose 23.3 percent to $2.93 billion, microelectronic products rose 18.3 percent to $615 million and business communications systems were up 14.1 percent to $1.3 billion.
The company said revenues from consumer products decreased 41 percent to $174 million, which it said was expected due to the restructuring of the business to increase profitability.

"We're delighted to report double-digit revenue growth and a dramatic quarter-over-quarter rise in profits as we complete our first year as a public company," Henry Schacht, Lucent's chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.

Network operator systems, or equipment used by telephone service carriers to run their operations, were led by strong sales of wireless systems, software, switching systems and professional services, the company said.
It said continued demand for second telephone lines in businesses and residences -- for uses such as Internet access, data traffic and faxing -- propelled the unit's performance.

U.S. domestic revenue from network operators rose about 21 percent in the second quarter, compared with the same period in 1996, led by sales to local Regional Bell service providers and non-traditional customers like wireless providers, competitive access providers, and cable television companies.

The group's international revenues rose about 32 percent and represented about 25 percent of the group's total revenues for the quarter, with increases in all major international regions. The results include higher sales of Lucent's 5ESS core carrier network switching systems and software in Japan.
Lucent said it benefited from strengthened relationships with the Regional Bell companies that have followed its spinoff from AT&T Corp a year ago.

This was demonstrated by its $1 billion switching equipment deal with Bell Atlantic Corp, an Ameritech Corp data equipment deal and a BellSouth Corp number portability software contract during the quarter.

In the past, local U.S. phone companies had previously been reticent to do business with the AT&T equipment arm, seeing AT&T as a potential rival in the coming era of open competition for local and long-distance services.

SBC Communications Inc's Southwestern Bell recently agreed to become the primary sales agent for Lucent's large business communications products in its traditional five-state region, a move it expected will generate higher revenues than each would realize without the relationship.

Gross margin for the quarter was 42.1 percent as a percentage of revenue, up from 39.9 percent in the comparable year-ago period, due primarily to the higher sales volume, benefits associated with productivity improvement initiatives and a favorable mix of product revenues.

Selling, general and administrative expenses declined to 25 percent as a percentage of revenues in the latest quarter from 29 percent in the comparable quarter of 1996. Research and development spending was 14.3 percent of revenues for the quarter, up 1.6 percent from a year ago due to greater investments in high growth areas like wireless systems, semiconductors and multimedia communications.
